author: Mark Atwood
text:
Three-way API-shape decision; needs human call.

Recommendation: option (c) — doc-only hardening in README Gotchas. Rationale:
  - Workspace policy on type crates already favors round-trip fidelity over construction-side strictness (Sloppy-Value pattern documented in workspace AGENTS.md, extras-preservation policy on every wire-format Deserialize struct).
  - The lib.rs:16-23 crate-level doc already commits to the lenient-Option philosophy. The bead's gap is documentation, not type-shape.
  - (a) doubles the type surface (every Calendar gets a CalendarStrict sibling); large breaking change to add later, but big API surface to land now.
  - (b) adds a method every caller must remember to invoke; a fresh-from-deserialize value carries no compile-time signal that validate() was called. The contract is easy to forget and the validation logic accumulates corner cases (Name "at least one of components or full", Organization "at least one of name or units", SpeakToAs "at least one of grammaticalGender or pronouns", OnlineService "at least one of uri or user", Address "at least one of components/full/coordinates/timeZone/countryCode", Author "at least one of name or uri").
  - (c) acknowledges the existing trade-off and tells consumers where to look. The crate ships as a wire-format mirror, not a validating builder.

If the human picks (a): big bead, file as a JMAP-sgrr.17.1 follow-up; will need to coordinate with the canonical-sibling jmap-jscalendar-types which has the same shape.

If the human picks (b): smaller bead, one validate() per type with mandatory or 'at-least-one' invariants; ~14 sites. ConstructionError shape needs design (probably an enum variant per field-pair). File as JMAP-sgrr.17.2.

If the human picks (c) [my recommendation]: I can land this in a single commit — add a Gotchas section to README and a doc-comment block on each affected struct cross-referencing the lib.rs:16-23 design statement.

The bead's status-quo phrase 'acceptable if and only if every downstream consumer duplicates the validation' is the real cost. (c) does not eliminate that cost; it just makes the duplication visible. (a) and (b) eliminate it at the price of locked-in API surface.
